title: Training-Free Linear Routing for Sparse Attention via Attention-Mass Prediction

contributions.purpose: Show that aligning query-key distributions geometrically is the wrong objective for training-free sparse-attention routing.
contributions.mechanism: Applies geometric moment matching via gauge-coupled whitening to align query and key distributions before symmetric k-means routing.
contributions.evaluation: Provides no improvement over symmetric k-means (50.7% vs 51.3% attention-mass recall on Qwen2.5-7B).
contributions.domain: Sparse attention routing for long-context LLM inference.
contributions.source_quote: (1) we demonstrate that geometric moment matching via gauge-coupled whitening provides no improvement over symmetric k-means, revealing that distribution alignment is the wrong objective

contributions.purpose: Provide a training-free router that approaches the quality of learned routers.
contributions.mechanism: GWR Linear predicts per-bucket attention mass via a closed-form ordinary least squares (OLS) linear predictor from calibration data, with no iterative optimization.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 72.6% attention-mass recall@32, closing 63.6% of the gap between symmetric k-means (51.3%) and a learned MLP router (84.8%).
contributions.domain: Sparse attention routing for long-context LLM inference.
contributions.source_quote: (2) we propose GWR Linear, achieving 63.6% gap closure to learned routing via closed-form OLS computation

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate the robustness/generalization of the proposed linear router.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluates GWR Linear across varying routing budgets and across multiple attention heads/layers.
contributions.evaluation: Gap closure ranges 44%-80% across routing budgets and averages 69.8% across 6 heads spanning layers 2-26.
contributions.domain: Sparse attention routing for long-context LLM inference.
contributions.source_quote: (3) we show that GWR Linear generalizes across routing budgets (44%-80% gap closure) and attention heads (mean 69.8% across 6 heads spanning layers 2-26)

self_declared_provenance.quote: Saap (Mazar'e et al., 2025) addresses the query-key distribution mismatch in pretrained models by training a per-head MLP router to select buckets for each query... Our work targets the same routing objective as Saap but achieves substantial quality via closed-form computation.

Our work is the first to achieve substantial gap closure to learned routing (63.6%) via a training-free closed-form approach, demonstrating that much of the routing signal can be captured by linear attention-mass prediction.

notes: Negative result: geometric moment matching (gauge-coupled whitening) provides no improvement over symmetric k-means (50.7% vs 51.3%), reported as C1 and framed as a key insight.
